Accelerates reindexing by up to 35-50% and IBD by 10-15% across varied hardware

result.summary: Adds an asynchronous block read-ahead mechanism (`BlockFetcher`) to `Chainstate` that prefetches up to 4 upcoming blocks using a 2-worker thread pool while previous blocks are being connected. The prefetcher also clears and warms its queue with sibling blocks during reorgs, avoiding redundant reads for caller-provided blocks.
result.problem: Block reading and deserialization historically happen synchronously right before block connection, preventing disk I/O from overlapping CPU-intensive validation during IBD, reindexing, and reorgs.

open_concerns: w0xlt suggested calling m_block_fetcher->Clear() when a block is found invalid so prefetched descendants do not linger in memory
resolved_concerns: Thread pool churn spamming logs on every ActivateBestChain call resolved by making Chainstate own the pool
Staged queue depth adjusted to 4 and workers to 2 following empirical benchmarking across SSD and HDD setups
Reorg sibling prefetching during DisconnectTip incorporated into the prefetch lifecycle
Circular dependency in build between blockfetcher and blockstorage resolved by using std::function

result.card: Adds a background BlockFetcher thread pool to Chainstate that reads and deserializes blocks ahead of ConnectTip, overlapping disk I/O with script and state validation. This directly benefits anyone performing initial sync or reindexing, with benchmarks demonstrating 12-15% faster IBD and 35-57% faster reindexing. Reviewer andrewtoth tested and ACKed after reproducing the performance gains, and the implementation is clean and ready for final review.
